title: A Princess Chooses Krishna
story:
The princess of Vidarbha settled her own marriage before anyone thought to ask her, and she settled it without ever having set eyes on the groom.

Rukmini was the daughter of Bhishmaka, king of Kundina, and she was known for her intelligence, her beauty, and her character. Her brother Rukmi had decided her future for her: he meant to give her in marriage to Shishupala, the king of Cedi, and as far as he was concerned the matter was closed. The girl herself was told that her hand was spoken for, and the household began to move toward the wedding as toward something already decided.

But Rukmini had been hearing other names. Word of Krishna of Dwaraka reached Kundina, and she listened to it closely, the way a thirsty field listens for rain. Travelers and brahmanas spoke of his beauty, of a valour that had grown into legend, of virtues and a glory that seemed to deepen with every telling. The more she heard, the more one conviction settled in her and would not be moved: he alone was a fitting husband for her. Not the prince her brother favored, not any of the alliances her family counted — Krishna.

She knew better than to take her wish to her family. Her brother had set his heart on Shishupala, and a princess who argued with him would only have tightened his grip on the plan. So Rukmini chose a different road. Among the brahmanas who traveled freely between the courts, carrying news and messages and blessings, she found one she trusted completely. To him she entrusted a message meant for Krishna and for no one else, and she sent him out swiftly and in secret, so that no word of her decision would reach her brother before the message reached its destination.

The brahmana took the long road from Vidarbha to Dwaraka and made it quickly, carrying the princess's secret like a flame cupped in his hands. At the city's gates he was admitted past the guards who kept them and brought to Krishna's presence.

And here the story turns on a small thing that says everything. When Krishna saw the travel-worn brahmana, he did not wait for the man to state his business. He rose from his own seat, a king rising for an unknown visitor, and received him as a guest of the first rank. For Krishna held the brahmanas in the highest honor; a man who had given his life to study and prayer came before any crown in his regard, and everyone in Dwaraka knew it.

The court watched the traveler be welcomed, given his place, spoken to with courtesy. And then the two of them spoke quietly together, and the message that had crossed the whole country on a princess's behalf passed out of the messenger's keeping and into Krishna's.

The brahmana had done what Rukmini asked of him. He had brought her decision to the one man in the world she had chosen — and what happened next would depend on Krishna's answer.
reflection: Rukmini chooses Krishna on report alone, before she has ever seen him, and she acts with startling practicality: where she cannot persuade her brother, she quietly arranges the matter herself through a trusted messenger. In this story the devotion begins with her, and it moves her to take her future into her own hands.
next_story_tease: What the brahmana had brought was no ordinary embassy: Rukmini had chosen her husband, and she meant for Krishna to know it.
hero_scene: A travel-worn brahmana standing before Krishna in the hall of Dwaraka while Krishna rises from his seat to receive him, the court watching in surprise as the unknown visitor is welcomed like a guest of the first rank.
